The off-market window

See it before everyone else does.

For now, 16 Viewbank Court is being offered quietly.

No realestate.com.au. No Domain. No signboard. No public open homes. The owners are simply giving a small number of buyers the chance to experience the property before the full campaign begins.

The first private viewing is Wednesday 7 October, from late afternoon into the evening — when the garden, the alfresco and the outdoor lighting really come into their own. A second private viewing follows on Saturday 10 October.

If the right buyer and the owners agree on terms during this window, the property may never need to reach the public market. Otherwise, the public campaign starts the following week.

Why this one

One family. One home. 37 years.

The owners bought the land and built their family home here in 1989, when the area was still known as Beenleigh Forest.

It is often the smaller, thoughtful details that reveal how a home has been lived in and cared for — the touches that make a house feel like a home. The home was designed and shaped by the family over time — the kitchen, laundry, alfresco, gardens, pavilion and studio all evolved with how they lived.

These were not last-minute sale improvements. They were changes made over decades by people who expected to stay.

The care is still evident today. The gardens and outdoor areas are established and ready to enjoy.

After 37 years with one family, the home is ready for an exciting new chapter.

Inside

A home improved for living, not for selling.

There is a difference between a house renovated for photographs and one improved gradually by the people living in it.

You can see that difference here.

  • The kitchenStone benchtops with matching stone splashbacks, Bosch appliances and remote-controlled under-cabinet lighting. It connects naturally with the dining room and the living area, so the everyday spaces sit together while remaining distinct.
  • The laundry, finished to the same standardThe renovation did not stop at the kitchen. The laundry has a stone benchtop, full-height cabinetry, overhead storage and direct external access to the side of the home.
  • Bathroom and separate WCThe bathroom is tiled floor to ceiling, with a large deep bath, a built-in bidet and Hansgrohe tapware. The WC is a separate room.
  • Three bedrooms, togetherAll three sit together away from the main entertaining areas, keeping the private part of the home separate from the spaces used for living and guests.
  • Finished and readyFresh internal paint, new internal doors and handles, and LED downlights through the kitchen and living areas.

The alfresco

Seventy-eight square metres, under roof.

Walk through the back of the house and the scale of 16 Viewbank Court starts to make sense.

The covered alfresco measures approximately 13 by 6 metres, extending almost the full width of the home.

It is a substantial outdoor living space that has been part of the way the family has used the home for decades — generous, established and designed to feel like an extension of the house. Designed for both larger gatherings and quieter family moments, 16 Viewbank Court offers a rare sense of privacy while giving you an extraordinary amount of outdoor space to enjoy.

And then the garden keeps going

Another place to gather, at the top of the garden.

Beyond the alfresco, the backyard rises through established landscaped terraces and stone retaining walls.

At the upper level is a second covered entertaining area — a substantial 6 by 6 metre garden pavilion, set privately among the landscaping. With its pitched timber-lined ceiling and tiled floor, it gives you another 36 m² of covered space away from the main house.

Morning coffee. A long lunch. Drinks with friends. Or simply another place to sit and enjoy the garden.

Together, the alfresco and the pavilion provide around 114 m² of covered outdoor living across two distinct areas. Both established, both finished, and both ready to enjoy from the day you move in.

The studio

Your own room, away from the house.

Tucked privately at the top of the garden is a detached studio of approximately 2.5 by 4 metres, lined and carpeted, with power, lighting and its own entrance.

Because it sits well away from the house, it works as an office, a music room, a gym, a quiet place to study, or a teenage retreat.

A proper room of your own, without giving up a bedroom inside the house.

Parking and access

Space for more than just the daily car.

The covered carport measures approximately 6.9 by 4 metres and sits behind an electric door. Alongside it is a further 4 by 6 metre concreted area, providing additional usable space beside the home.

Two side gates provide direct access to the backyard from either side of the home, which is one of those practical details that makes the property work especially well day to day, which is one of those practical details that makes the property work especially well day to day.

There is also a garden shed.

Simple things, but the kind that make a home easier to live in.

Comfort, security and the jobs already done

Cared for and improved over the years.

The home has been cared for from the inside out, with years of practical upgrades to the systems, security and everyday features that make the property comfortable to live in. Meticulously maintained and thoughtfully modernised, it reflects decades of pride in ownership and careful attention to the details that matter. Years of diligent upkeep and considered updates mean much of the work has already been done, leaving a home that is ready to enjoy.

The land

617 m² that has been thoughtfully planned and established.

The 617 m² block is thoughtfully landscaped, well used and established.

The owners have shaped the backyard into a series of usable landscaped levels, held by stone retaining walls. The house opens to the alfresco. The alfresco opens to the garden. The garden rises toward the pavilion and the detached studio. Each area connects naturally with the next while still having a purpose of its own.

The landscaping is mature yet easy to maintain, with lush established gardens providing shade, greenery and privacy.

The garden is beautifully established after decades of care. The expansive backyard also gives future owners space to consider how the property might evolve further over time, whether through additional outdoor features or future additions, subject of course to the relevant approvals.

Where it is

A quiet cul-de-sac to come home to.

Viewbank Court is a small cul-de-sac with little reason for through traffic, which gives the street a noticeably quieter feel than a main suburban road.

It is the kind of position you tend to appreciate more once you live there, particularly with children, pets, or simply a preference for a little less traffic outside the front door.

Beenleigh’s shops, schools, train station and everyday services are only minutes away, while access to the M1 makes travelling north toward Brisbane or south toward the Gold Coast straightforward.

Close to what you need. Quiet when you come home.
